purpose_and_scope.project_purpose: Windows deployment manager for preparing, building, publishing, diagnosing and deploying ASP.NET Core web applications to local or remote IIS with reusable dependency repositories, SQL Server preparation, rollback/health checks and offline-capable workflows.
in_scope: Windows Forms deployment wizard and settings UI
SQL Server discovery, installation assistance and database connectivity
Build/deployment diagnostics, history, performance and runtime metrics
Fast/local/full deployment modes, rollback and health checks
Self-build/release scripts for Deployment Manager itself
out_of_scope: Application-specific business logic of deployed products
Destructive modification of deployed application business data without explicit approval
Treating temporary/versioned incoming source folders as persistent dependency repositories
success_criteria: A user can select a source, pass automatic source preflight, prepare dependencies and deploy with clear status and diagnostics.
Reusable dependencies survive deletion of versioned incoming source folders.
Release output is written to the configured Manager release/output folder as both DeploymentManager.exe and a versioned executable.
Failures are logged with useful diagnostics while secrets are not persisted in project profiles/log output.
Every software version is accompanied by an aligned Project Evolution record.
source_of_truth_notes: Actual Source is authoritative for implementation claims.
Runtime/user confirmation is required for runtime acceptance.
PES-1 records durable intent, decisions, state, evidence and history.

handoff_policy.rule: Any durable continuation knowledge must be committed to PE before release close.

Use stable IDs and relationships; never silently rewrite history.

decisions.title: Adopt aligned PES-1 release governance
decisions.decision: From V57 onward, software version and Project Evolution version are aligned in the same release cycle.
decisions.reason: The user wants the full architecture, decisions, analysis, runtime state and release history to travel with every Source release.
alternatives_considered: Start PE at V1 while software continues at V57
consequences: Every release updates two artifacts: Source ZIP and aligned PE JSON.
PES standard stays PES-1 until the standard itself changes.

decisions.title: Separate temporary Source, persistent repository and stable workspace
decisions.decision: Incoming Source is treated as temporary/versioned; dependency packages live in Shared Dependency Repository; build working files live in Stable Build Workspace.
decisions.reason: Incoming version folders may be deleted after deployment and must not be the only dependency/cache source.
alternatives_considered: Use incoming Source as dependency-sync source/store
consequences: Workspace preserves node_modules/bin/obj for incremental builds.

decisions.title: Diagnostics exports are files, not folder-selection workflows
decisions.decision: Use explicit ZIP files for tab/all diagnostic exports. Desktop is the default one-click destination; alternate destinations use SaveFileDialog.
decisions.reason: The previous folder-picker workflow made Desktop selection and the final export location unclear to the operator.
alternatives_considered: Keep FolderBrowserDialog and show a success path
consequences: Export location is deterministic and visible.
Users can open the file or containing folder immediately.
ProgramData remains internal runtime storage rather than the normal user export destination.

findings.user_statement: Owner supplied V58 build screenshot showing restore failure because generated path exceeded the Windows 260-character path limit.
findings.expected_behavior: Release build succeeds regardless of a long incoming/versioned source folder name.
findings.actual_behavior: V58 restore failed before publish when building directly under the long source path.
findings.observation: MSBuild/NuGet reported fully qualified generated publish path must be less than 260 characters.
findings.source_inspection_result: V58 build-release scripts restored/published directly from the source tree.
findings.root_cause: Self-release scripts used the incoming source path as the build root, allowing generated paths to exceed legacy MAX_PATH.
findings.implementation_result: Both release scripts now stage source under %LOCALAPPDATA%\GWDM\Build\V59 before restore/publish.

findings.user_statement: V59 deployment failed during Vite build with Could not resolve entry module index.html.
findings.expected_behavior: Deployment Manager must select the real source frontend regardless of drive letter or generated publish folders.
findings.actual_behavior: V59 selected IIS-Publish/ClientApp, a generated publish tree without index.html, instead of src/NSPOffice.Api/ClientApp.
findings.observation: Diagnostic bundle and runtime screenshot established two ClientApp candidates; generated IIS-Publish candidate was incorrectly selected.
findings.source_inspection_result: V59 FindClientFolder excluded common generated folders but did not exclude IIS-Publish/publish; selection preferred first package.json with a build script.
findings.root_cause: Frontend discovery did not classify IIS-Publish/publish as generated output and did not score complete Vite source roots.
findings.implementation_result: Generated IIS-Publish/publish paths excluded; candidate selection now requires build script and scores index.html + vite.config.*; preflight reports the selected complete Vite root.

findings.user_statement: Diagnostic bundle captured SQL integrated-auth warning during deployment.
findings.expected_behavior: Administrative SQL connection diagnostics should distinguish authentication/environment warnings from deployment-blocking failures.
findings.actual_behavior: Automatic administrative connection test reported untrusted domain / Integrated authentication warning while deployment continued.
findings.observation: Not the cause of the V59 frontend build failure; retained for later analysis.

findings.user_statement: Owner supplied a handoff requiring IIS-Publish to be treated as final prepared output and never as project source.
findings.expected_behavior: Prepared IIS Publish validates the prebuilt artifact then deploys it to IIS without npm, Vite, dependency restore, dotnet build or dotnet publish.
findings.actual_behavior: Prior workflow could still enter source/frontend build behavior around IIS-Publish and treated ClientApp inside publish output as source.
findings.observation: NSP Office GitHub Actions already produces validated IIS-Publish with BUILD-METADATA.json; runtime_acceptance may remain PENDING.
findings.source_inspection_result: V60 already had a Ready/Prepared branch but validation was weak, UI location was split, prepared deployment still generated source fingerprint state and post-deploy verification expected smart-build state.
findings.root_cause: Prepared publish existed as a partial mode rather than a fully isolated execution contract.
findings.implementation_result: Prepared IIS Publish is explicit on Source page; validates web.config + app binary + wwwroot + optional BUILD-METADATA PASS fields; source dependency controls are disabled; PublishAsync hard-bypasses build stages; post-deploy verification validates prepared output rather than source fingerprints; configured production appsettings files are preserved from rollback copy.

findings.user_statement: Owner supplied V61 runtime screenshot showing deployment failure because C:\inetpub\wwwroot.__rollback already existed.
findings.expected_behavior: Every deployment backup is collision-safe, prepared before IIS downtime, and can restore the exact previous hosted state.
findings.actual_behavior: V61 used a fixed sibling rollback directory and attempted to create/move into it, causing deployment failure when a stale rollback directory already existed.
findings.observation: V61 reached IIS deployment but failed at backup preparation with Cannot create C:\inetpub\wwwroot.__rollback because a file or directory with the same name already exists.
findings.source_inspection_result: V61 GetRollbackFolder returned HostingRoot + .__rollback; deletion failure was logged but deployment then attempted Directory.Move into the still-existing path.
findings.root_cause: Rollback identity was global/fixed rather than per deployment, and stale rollback cleanup was non-fatal even though subsequent move required the path to be absent.
findings.implementation_result: V62 creates timestamp+GUID backups under DeploymentRoot/Backups/Application, copies and validates backup before IIS stop, restores from the active unique backup on failure, and retains newest five backups.
